data.name: Batinun
data.gender_notes: Batinun is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who is hidden, the concealed one, the secret one. Derived from the Arabic root 'batana' which means 'to cover, conceal, hide'. The name Batinun carries the meaning “Hidden one, concealed” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Batinun usually hope their child will grow to embody hidden one, concealed and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It can also be seen as a symbol of the hidden knowledge and wisdom that can be accessed through introspection and spiritual practice.
data.etymology: Batinun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Hidden one, concealed.”

in_arabic.name: بطينون

in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم بطينون مشتق من الجذر العربي ب-ط-ن، ويشير إلى باطن الشيء أو جوهره الداخلي. ورد في القرآن الكريم في سياق الحديث عن الأسماء الحسنى لله عز وجل، ودل على صفة من صفات الله تعالى التي تعبر عن علمه الباطن والشامل لجميع الأشياء. يستخدم الاسم في الثقافة الإسلامية ليدل على العمق والفهم الداخلي للأمور

in_urdu.name: بطینون
in_urdu.meaning: نام کا مطلب ہے کسی چیز کا باطن یا اندرونی جوہر
in_urdu.long_meaning: بطینون نام عربی جڑ ب-ط-ن سے ماخوذ ہے، جو کسی چیز کے باطن یا اندرونی جوہر کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ قرآن مجید میں اس کا ذکر الله کے خوبصورت ناموں کے تناظر میں کیا گیا ہے، اور یہ الله کی ایک صفت کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے جو تمام چیزوں کے بارے میں باطنی علم رکھتا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلم معاشرے میں، یہ نام کسی چیز کی داخلیت یا گہری سمجھ کو ظاہر کرنے کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے

in_english.long_meaning: The name Batinun is derived from the Arabic root ب-ط-ن (b-ṭ-n), which refers to the inner essence or the internal substance of something. In the context of Islamic tradition and the Quran, this name alludes to one of Allah's attributes, signifying His comprehensive and intimate knowledge of all things. The name holds spiritual significance, representing depth and profound understanding. Across Muslim cultures, Batinun is used to denote inner wisdom and deep insight into matters

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic philosophy and mysticism (Sufism), the term "Batin" (Hidden or Concealed) is used to describe the deeper, inner, esoteric aspects of things, versus the superficial, outer, exoteric meanings. This dichotomy between the Hidden and theManifested in Islamic culture is analogous to the difference between the "shar'i" (legislative or legal) and the "haqiqi" (real or true) in Islamic jurisprudence. It's an ongoing reminder of the higher truth that often lies unseen beneath the surface of things.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, "Batinun" is the embodiment of the spiritual seeker, who strives to uncover the deeper truths hidden beneath the surface of life, the universe, and even the self. This reflection of the hidden and the concealed is a reminder of the greater reality that surpasses the surface-level experiences and perceptions of the physical world. Therefore, Batinun signifies the quest for self-awareness, self-realization, and the ultimate union with the Divine (Tawhid).
